official_scoring_enabled_note: Fail-closed until the Laguna go-live: hidden goldens, the paired M5 baseline, and the weight manifests must be regenerated on m5-bench with the real Laguna weights (new tokenizer, vocab 100352) before the enablement commit flips this to true, and the token_fidelity_gate below must be fully specified (the DFlash go-live runbook supersedes the retired docs/mtp-track-golive-runbook.md, which was removed with the MTP track).
timed_prompt_pool_note: Contract layer L6 (anti-lottery). The timed target is sampled UNIFORMLY AT RANDOM from this pool once per ranked run, from kernel entropy the participant cannot see or influence; the selected index is recorded only in the private audit dir. A single frozen timed prompt would make a failed ranked run free to retry, degrading every output-side gate into submit-until-green and letting a drafter-confidence threshold be tuned across resubmissions; sampling from a pool of N reduces that to a 1/N chance per attempt. Each entry must be an object {r2_path, sha256, bytes} and is verified byte-for-byte after download. DELIBERATELY EMPTY: the selection step in .github/workflows/dflash-benchmark.yml fails CLOSED on an empty pool, exactly as the weight manifests did before they were regenerated on-box. Populate this with at least 8 distinct hidden timed targets (varied prompt length and domain, so acceptance-rate tuning cannot generalise) before flipping official_scoring_enabled. Hashes are only ever pinned from the uploaded objects, never pre-filled off-box.

protocol.name: trusted_dflash_block_v1
protocol.maximum_block_size_note: Raised from 4 (Gemma-MTP assistant era) to 16: the DFlash draft model's config block_size is 16 and it drafts a whole masked block in one forward. SUPERSEDED MEASUREMENT: an earlier note here claimed peak decode speedup at K=8 (1.60x) with K=16 at 1.53x. Those came from short and/or self-generated prompts and do NOT reproduce at the frozen window. Measured at a 512-token seed over 128 decode steps with matched token counts on both sides: on varied prose, draft acceptance is 69% and K=4 is 0.840x, i.e. SLOWER than serial; on a degenerate greedy self-continuation (122 distinct tokens in 512) acceptance is ~100% and K=4 is 1.117x. A verify row costs only ~10% less than a standalone serial step, so break-even needs draft acceptance above ~92%. K remains a runtime choice bounded by this maximum, but do not read the maximum as a recommendation.
protocol.decode_tokens_note: The RANKED decode window, in parent-counted tokens. Was 128 (inherited from the retired track's local-iterate default) while proposed_scoring.ranked_decode_window_tokens and benchmark.dflash.json scoring.decodeTokens both said 512 -- three places disagreeing about the scored window. All three must stay equal; DFlashTrackTests pins that. maximum_decode_tokens (1536) remains the protocol ceiling, and the local scripts use their own smaller values for directional runs.

reference_baseline._note: The paired serial K=1 baseline, floor calibration, and hidden goldens for Laguna XS 2.1 must be established on m5-bench before this flips to established/publication_allowed=true (go-live runbook steps B-C).

proposed_scoring.aggregation: ratio_of_means: mean(serial seconds/token across accepted pairs) / mean(dflash seconds/token across accepted pairs)
proposed_scoring.paired_serial_reference: trusted serial K=1 target decode (probe path) over the same golden, same session, same thermal gate, same box
proposed_scoring.denominator_authority: trusted parent wall time divided by the parent-configured decode total
proposed_scoring.component_floor: aggregate dflash_decode_speedup >= 0.80 (floor applies to the ratio-of-means aggregate, not per pair). Set by operator decision 2026-07-30, DELIBERATELY NOT 1.0. On this track 1.0 is not the no-change line: block decode itself costs about 16% on realistic prose, because a verify row is only ~10% cheaper than a standalone serial step and at 69% draft acceptance the block path declares 1.25 rows per emitted token. A submission that changes NOTHING scores 0.840x at the frozen window (512-token seed, 128 decode steps, matched token counts on both sides; the same measurement gives 1.117x on a degenerate greedy self-continuation, which is why earlier sweeps looked healthy -- correctness contract Amendments 10, 11 and 21). Because the denominator is a clone of the PINNED baseline and only the numerator is the candidate's build, general kernel improvements DO move the score, so a floor at 1.0 would not reject regressions -- it would reject every submission whose kernel improvement is under about 19%, including honest 10% wins, which is this track's stated purpose. 0.80 is the unmodified-candidate score with room for run-to-run variation: a no-op sits just above the floor and any real kernel gain ranks. MAX_PLAUSIBLE_SPEEDUP stays 5.0. This value must stay equal to scoring.decodeSpeedupFloor in benchmark.dflash.json (pinned by a test) and to MIN_ACCEPTED_SPEEDUP in /opt/bench-runner/measure-dflash-job.sh on every box serving this track.
proposed_scoring.token_fidelity_gate: PENDING SPEC (supersedes the Gemma-MTP bit_exact_gate). The MTP-era criterion -- every returned token must exactly match the trusted SEQUENTIAL oracle -- is empirically unachievable for DFlash on Laguna NVFP4: the target's own block-shaped forward diverges from K sequential forwards at near-tie argmax positions with NO drafter involved (measured on M5 2026-07-30: 14/14 divergences were target block-vs-sequential; max sequential-logit gap 0.625; 12/14 were sequential rank 2, one rank 3, one rank 5 in a flat distribution). The replacement criterion is trusted sequential re-verification with a bounded near-tie budget; exact values are being specified separately and MUST be written here before official_scoring_enabled can flip to true.
proposed_scoring.stall_guardrail: a run whose max block latency exceeds 4x its p50 block latency is rejected as measurement-invalid with one gated retry
proposed_scoring.prefill_component: none; seed prefill is charged inside the decode measurement
proposed_scoring.leaderboard: separate laguna-xs-2.1-dflash-v1 namespace, never mixed with the serial track
proposed_scoring.measurement_protocol: minimum three accepted thermal-gated pairs per session (target four) with alternating order; single-pair scores are not publishable
